title: Telemetry intake sparkline and graceful rejection
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: We see intermittent spikes of malformed usage events in the Console telemetry intake that cause downstream consumers (billing, analytics, and alerting pipelines) to fail or produce noisy metrics. Root causes vary: truncated payloads from mobile SDKs, new optional fields added by feature flags, and occasional double-encoded JSON from legacy integrations. Goals: (1) Implement a lightweight, high-throughput probe stage in the intake path that performs fast structural checks and schema compatibility scoring; (2) Provide graceful rejection and routing so bad events don't cascade into downstream systems; (3) Emit a sparkline/mini-timeseries and sampled payloads for rapid debugging; (4) Keep per-request latency impact <1ms p95 at normal load and ensure the intake can be toggled to strict or permissive mode per-route.
acceptance_criteria: A fast validation probe runs in the edge ingestion path and adds <=1ms p95 latency under normal traffic
Malformed events are rejected with a well-typed error envelope and an assigned rejection code; downstream pipelines continue to operate
A sparkline metric (ingest.validation.failure_rate) is emitted per route with 10s resolution and visible in the console dashboard
Sampled payloads for failures (1:1000 default) are stored in a short-lived debug bucket with a retention of 7 days and linked from the console errors UI
Configuration: per-route validation mode (disabled | permissive | strict), sample rate override, and a circuit-breaker for backpressure
E2E tests and a load test demonstrating behavior under synthetic malformed flood and normal traffic
tasks: Design validation probe API (handlers + non-blocking schema score) — Miguel
Add rejection envelope format and update downstream adapters to tolerate new error shape — Data Eng
Implement sparkline metric and dashboard tile in Console — Product/Observability
Build sampled payload archiver (s3://redwood-debug/ingest-samples/) with TTL — Infra
Create feature flag to flip permissive <-> strict per-route — Platform
Write load tests (k6) to assert <1ms p95 latency overhead — SRE
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Kapoor: Spiked this after investigating Friday's billing pipeline noise. Initial telemetry shows ~0.6% malformed rate on new SDK release channels. We need a short-term stopgap that avoids dropping legitimate events from older SDK versions.

2025-02-12 Miguel Torres: Prototype probe implemented in a feature branch. Uses a fast JSON shape check + small schema fingerprint heuristic. Local benchmark: +0.7ms p95 on my dev box at 5000 QPS equiv. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/428

2025-02-13 Product feedback (Lena Park): Make sure rejection envelope includes the event id, route, and a human-readable hint. The console errors UI will link directly to sampled payloads; include a sample_id in the envelope.

2025-02-15 Design note (Eli Martinez): For the sparkline UI we want a 60s rolling window by default and an additional mini-heatmap by route. I'll file a DES ticket to prototype the tile. UX constraints: avoid exposing raw payloads unless user has permission.

2025-02-16 Miguel Torres: Added circuit-breaker to auto-switch the probe to permissive mode if validation CPU > 80% or failure rate > 20% for 30s. Verified behavior in staging; added metrics ingest.validation.probe_mode with values [disabled, permissive, strict].

2025-02-18 SRE (Noah Chen): Ran k6 flood test simulating malformed payload injection. System maintained p95 latency under target when probe in permissive; strict mode caused increased backpressure as expected. Recommend default permissive for 2 weeks rolling deploy.

2025-02-19 Aisha Kapoor: PM approved default rollout plan: start permissive on all routes for 24 hours, then enable strict on low-risk routes (console-read, embeddings-read) and monitor for 72h before broader strict enforcement.

2025-02-20 Miguel Torres: Preparing RFC/PR for main with tracking dashboard and infra job to clear samples older than 7 days. Targeting merge and canary on 2025-02-25. Follow-ups: automated repair path for double-encoded JSON (ENG-FOLLOWUP-1).
notes: Trade-offs: strict mode provides cleaner downstream data but increases risk of customer-facing drops. Permissive mode attaches a validation_score and lets consumers decide; strict mode rejects early and reduces downstream noise.
Follow-ups: (a) schema fuzzing job to proactively find new field combos before SDK releases, (b) integration with the onboarding catalog to auto-whitelist known legacy payload shapes.
Security: Sampled payloads are redacted for PII and only accessible to users with debug-data role. Infra job includes KMS encryption at rest.
